races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap

runners_data.name: Belicoso
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's hold-up juvenile has finished 3rd at 7f on good ground and represents an OR-drop from 81 — the step to a mile could suit his waiting style, but he needs a genuinely strong pace from the front-running pair to deliver his finish and has yet to win.|

runners_data.name: Margot Mae
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the ride for Harrington on this confirmed front-runner who has been off 43 days — limited placed form on good ground and an OR of 78 means she is likely to battle Seaxburh for the lead, yet her best finish here was a 3rd at 7f on soft, and raw front-running ability may not stretch a full mile.|

runners_data.name: Seaxburh
runners_data.note: O'Brien's filly is the most reliable horse in the race by placed-form record, with three seconds and a third across five starts all on good ground and two at 8f — wearing headgear (p) and dropping only marginally in the weights, she should dispute or sit just off the pace and her course-distance profile is the strongest in the field.|

runners_data.name: Razmataz
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's juvenile carries a late-fade flag supported by finishes of 11th, 8th, and 15th — low OR of 70 and a string of poor efforts on good ground make this a speculative entry, and there is little in his form to suggest he can reverse these trends even with pace collapse.|

runners_data.name: Maggie Walker
runners_data.note: Marnane's filly won on soft over 6f at her most recent start and has been off 55 days — her true running style is deep hold-up, but with multiple closers in this field she is unlikely to settle as far back as natural, meaning she races in a compromised position, and her single win came on softer going than today's good surface.|

runners_data.name: Old Joanie
runners_data.note: Unknown style (U-rated) for Barrett with a 5-claimer aboard and a 27-day gap since last run — all three recent efforts have been on good ground at 7f and she has shown mid-race consistency without threatening the frame, so the step to a mile and the contested gallop are genuine unknown quantities here.|

runners_data.name: Elyatta
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's gelding carries both a late-fade warning and a redistribution flag — his true instinct is to race from the rear, yet in a field crowded with hold-up types he is unlikely to secure that ground-saving position; three finishes of 9th, 8th, and 10th on good ground underline that improvement is needed before tactics matter.|

runners_data.name: Fine Line
runners_data.note: Hogan's juvenile has a sequence of 7th, 10th, 10th, 12th and another fade flag — a natural closer who cannot get his preferred position in this race shape, and at OR 63 the ceiling here looks modest; Chris Hayes takes the ride but the form evidence across four good-ground starts does not encourage confidence in any scenario.|

races.paceDynamic: Margot Mae and Seaxburh are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested pace over this flat Killarney mile on good ground — neither is likely to concede without a fight, so an honest, pressure-driven gallop from the outset is the most probable script. That sustained early tempo will stretch the field and drain finishing reserves, meaning horses that travel smoothly just off the pace in the prominent-to-midfield berth — rather than those making up ground from a cold hold-up position — are best placed to exploit the final furlong. Belicoso is the standout hold-up operator in the race but will need the pace to truly collapse the field ahead of him; his chance hinges on the gallop being genuinely searching rather than falsely run. This field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Maggie Walker, Elyatta, and Fine Line are all true deep closers but have been redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning they are unlikely to get their natural ground-saving position and their effectiveness as late finishers is materially compromised. The race shape strongly favours a prominent-tracking runner who can sit just behind the contested lead and pounce when the pace-setters tie up in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Margot Mae and Seaxburh fight for the front and set a genuine searching gallop that exposes both pace-setters in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The contested pace burns up the leaders and opens the door for a horse settled just behind them — Seaxburh's consistent placed form at 7f-8f on good ground suggests she has the tactical speed to track and rally, while Old Joanie, running from an unknown style profile, could emerge if she finds a prominent position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Margot Mae gains a soft lead or Seaxburh breaks faster and the contested duel resolves early into one clear front-runner dictating a controlled pace.
scenarios.body: With the pace pressure easing, the leader conserves enough energy to hold on up the straight, and at Killarney's flat mile a horse that has already been competitive over 7f-8f on good ground is best placed — Seaxburh's three placed efforts at this trip and going combination make her the prime candidate, with Margot Mae the alternative if she clears the break cleanly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough to open a meaningful gap in the straight and a true closer can thread through a strung-out field.
scenarios.body: Belicoso is the only genuine unrelocated hold-up type in this field and his best form of 3rd at 7f on good ground shows he can finish, though stepping to a mile is an unknown — he needs the pace to be searingly honest and a clear run through beaten horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners cancel each other out early, the pace collapses mid-race and the field concertinas turning for home.
scenarios.body: A bunched finish over the final furlong advantages the horse with the highest raw ability regardless of position, and in that scramble Razmataz — despite worrying late-fade flags — could find himself carried into contention off a flat, even-tempo second half; Maggie Walker, despite being out of natural position, has won previously and holds residual each-way claims if she can slot in comfortably.

watchPoints.text: Seaxburh and Margot Mae will lock horns for the lead from the off — watch the opening quarter-mile to see which one concedes, as the horse that gets the uncontested front dramatically improves its prospects of lasting the full mile.

Maggie Walker, Elyatta, and Fine Line are all natural hold-up horses who will be squeezed out of their preferred ground-saving positions — if any of the three gets shuffled wide or back early, their chance of landing a blow in the straight is severely reduced.

Belicoso's finishing effort is entirely dependent on the pace remaining honest throughout — if either front-runner eases off significantly through the middle portion of the race, his hold-up run from the rear will not generate enough momentum to catch the leaders.

Old Joanie's unknown style rating is a genuine wildcard — watch where Rory Mulligan slots her in the early stages, as a prominent position on the fence could give her a ground-saving route into contention that her form figures do not fully advertise.

Razmataz's late-fade flag has been consistent across all three starts; if he is pushed forward early by Gavin Ryan to secure a position, monitor whether he is already off the bridle entering the back straight, as that would confirm the pace is searingly honest and benefits the prominent trackers.

races.name: CSG Rated Race

runners_data.name: Mayflower
runners_data.note: A hold-up filly who won over this trip on Soft but is 0-from-5 in similar going and 0-from-4 in her recent form string; Jack Kearney claims 3lb but will need an unusually strong pace to generate the late surge her style demands in a race where the front-runner faces no pressure.

runners_data.name: Do For Love
runners_data.note: 127 days off is a notable absence and soft-to-standard form dominates the history, but Gary Carroll's experience for K J Condon (0/8 T14) and a win at this trip suggests she can slot into the prominent position she needs if fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Kirkland Sioux
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over one mile on Good ground is the standout recent form in this field, and Dylan Browne McMonagle retains the ride for a trainer running at a 12% T14 strike-rate; should secure the prominent berth just off the leader that suits him perfectly.

runners_data.name: Manton Bay
runners_data.note: An adaptable profile — won over a mile, placed over longer — that allows Luke McAteer to make an early decision whether to chase the pace or drop in; Good going is fine, but the trainer's 0/14 T14 returns temper enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Oscar Nominee
runners_data.note: Only two runs on record, both at ten furlongs on Standard, so the drop to a mile on Good turf is a significant unknown; Ben Coen is a major positive and both efforts to date were close-up, suggesting the prominent position suits, but data is thin.

runners_data.name: Iamimmaculate
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners a horse who wants to race prominently — placed twice in five starts — but with Kirkland Sioux, Do For Love, and Oscar Nominee ahead in the queue for those spots, he is likely to find himself in a midfield position that does not play to his strengths; 1/8 T14 for O'Leary is moderate.

runners_data.name: Totally Puzzled
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this exact trip on Good ground at Killarney, gives Ronan Whelan a gift position on the front end with no pace rival in sight; 96 days off is the one query but De Bromhead's yard is firing (4/38 T14) and the hg:h headgear is retained.

runners_data.name: Elmakaya
runners_data.note: Consistent form figure of 7-2-3-4 in four Good-ground runs at this trip, and D K Weld always merits respect, but this is another horse whose natural inclination is to race prominently and the overcrowded pace map means Chris Hayes will struggle to get him where he wants to be.

races.paceDynamic: Totally Puzzled is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will ease into a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front on Good ground at Killarney over one mile. Do For Love, Kirkland Sioux, and Oscar Nominee will press into prominent positions behind the leader, but the absence of pace pressure means Totally Puzzled sets an honest rather than searching tempo — the kind that keeps rivals travelling within themselves rather than forcing them to burn energy chasing. The hold-up operator Mayflower will have to rely on an insufficient injection of pace to generate the gaps she needs late on, while Manton Bay's versatile style gives her options to sit just off the pace. This field holds more prominent types than the shape can accommodate: Do For Love, Kirkland Sioux, Oscar Nominee, Iamimmaculate, and Elmakaya all want to race up with the pace, but only two or three positions exist — Kirkland Sioux (most recent form, in-form trainer) and Do For Love are likeliest to actually secure those berths, with Iamimmaculate and Elmakaya shuffled back against their natural preference. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can sit on or just behind the leader's shoulder and produce a sustained run into the straight — the prominent-to-lead profile wins here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Totally Puzzled Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Totally Puzzled dictates a moderate, uncontested pace and quickens off the bend to hold every challenger.
scenarios.body: Ronan Whelan sets his own rhythm from the front, and with no rival willing or able to push the pace, the tempo is controlled enough to preserve plenty of reserves for the Killarney straight; a horse at the front meeting no pressure on Good ground over a flat mile is hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pouncers Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough that one of the prominent horses tracking Totally Puzzled picks up sharply to collar the leader inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Kirkland Sioux or Do For Love, sitting a length or two off the gallop, produces a decisive turn of foot off the final bend and runs past a leader who has perhaps gone just a stride too soon; Kirkland Sioux's back-to-back wins at this trip on Good and his powerful stable make him the most credible threat in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Versatile Type Sneaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough to compress the field and a track-position switch by Manton Bay or Oscar Nominee delivers an unexpected winner from just off the pace.
scenarios.body: A compressed field on a moderate tempo means the straight becomes messy, and a horse like Manton Bay — with wins and places at this trip on similar going — threads through gaps that a conventional hold-up runner cannot exploit; Oscar Nominee's limited form makes the unknown quantity a wildcard rather than a banker.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the front two or three tire badly, allowing Mayflower or Iamimmaculate to finish through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because Totally Puzzled is uncontested and will not burn herself out, and Iamimmaculate — a natural prominent racer displaced to midfield by the redistribution — is not a true closer and will not get the late run this shape demands; Mayflower's 0-from-5 in similar conditions further undermines confidence in this outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Kirkland Sioux gets a clear prominent position early — if Dylan Browne McMonagle is forced wide or back by the cluster of prominent types, his winning chance is meaningfully reduced.

Totally Puzzled's 96-day absence is the main unknown for the probable leader; if she is ring-rusty early and drops away rounding the final bend, the entire pace map collapses and the scenario probabilities shift sharply toward Scenario B or C.

Monitor Do For Love's market and pre-race behaviour given 127 days off — a horse returning from a long layoff in a prominent style on ground faster than most of her best form is a vulnerability that the odds may not fully price.

Elmakaya and Iamimmaculate are both natural prominent racers crowded out of their preferred position — if either drifts further back than planned, back-to-back scrimmaging in the early stages could compromise both their runs and the overall pace picture.

Oscar Nominee's step back in trip from ten to eight furlongs on turf Good for the first time is worth monitoring in the market; any late confidence from the Murtagh yard (2/28 T14) could signal improved fitness after 165 days off.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Vincent O'Brien Ruby Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Cristal Clere
runners_data.note: Front-runner who brings strong place form on Good ground (2nd in a 13f Good race), but the step back to 1m on this track suits her pace profile; 63 days off is a minor question and trainer Nallen is quiet recently at 0/3 in 14 days.|

runners_data.name: East Hampton
runners_data.note: True hold-up sprinter stepping up to 1m from a career spent over 6-7f, making this a significant and unproven trip; David Marnane's yard has been busy but quiet (0/14), and six back is a formidable draw at Killarney without proven stamina.|

runners_data.name: Jagged Edge
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who landed a Goodwood 8f win (OR level) and handles Good ground well (7/9 sim-going), making him a genuine threat to sit close and sustain; the 19-day turnaround is no concern and Kearney is a booking worth noting in a Listed field.|

runners_data.name: Carolina Jetstream
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who was second over this exact trip in Good ground (2/8f/GOO), and De Aguiar's yard is alive with two wins in 14 days; the 55-day break is the only mild reservation, though she returns to her optimum distance.|

runners_data.name: Quebec
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from the powerful O'Brien yard, returning after 89 days and stepping to a mile where she has struggled (4/7 sim-going, no wins); Declan McDonogh takes over but the layoff and weak 1m record make this a difficult assignment.|

runners_data.name: Rion Rubette
runners_data.note: Dual 7f Good-ground winner who has shown sharp speed on her winning days — her natural racing style is more forward than the midfield slot suggests, as the field's volume of hold-up types displaced her rearward on the map; the 14-day turnaround is fine and Butler's horses run honestly.|

runners_data.name: Subsonic
runners_data.note: John Murtagh's filly carries a hood (tp) and has a 10f pedigree profile that makes 1m potentially too sharp; her true hold-up style is compressed into a midfield position on the map because of field congestion at the rear, meaning she likely can't produce her best hold-up run here.|

runners_data.name: Syzygy
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has produced three placed efforts over 8-9f Good ground and wears a hood (b) suggesting she can be keen; McLoughlin has her consistent but the 36-day break is fine, and she needs the pace to be real to have a chance off her true hold-up style.|

runners_data.name: Hardy Warrior
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old front-runner wearing a tongue-tie (tp), trained by the red-hot O'Brien yard (7/57); won over 8f on Soft, handled Good, and DBM is a major jockey asset — the key question is whether he can handle the immediate lead challenge from Cristal Clere.|

runners_data.name: Moonlit Sun
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old who won on debut over 8f Good for Harrington and has three runs to her name (3/3 sim-going), but she is a genuine hold-up filly whose natural late style will be harder to execute from the midfield berth the map allocates due to field congestion; Shane Foley is a positive booking.|

runners_data.name: Wearing Stars
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's three-year-old wears a tongue-tie (t) and has produced back-to-back 2nds over 8f Good ground, making her course-and-distance profile compelling; she tracks from midfield and her consistency suggests she won't be far away if given a clear run in the straight.|

races.paceDynamic: Hardy Warrior and Cristal Clere are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this flat Killarney mile, creating an honest, consistently-run gallop on Good ground. That contested pace is unlikely to produce a truly gruelling early burn, but it will be genuine enough to stretch the field and compress finishing time, favouring horses that can travel prominently without burning their reserves. Prominent types Carolina Jetstream and Jagged Edge are best placed to exploit a genuinely-run race by sitting just off the duelling leaders and pouncing in the straight. This race shape — a contested but not chaotic lead — most clearly suits prominent racers who can control their position, rather than deep closers who need the pace to collapse. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Subsonic, Rion Rubette, and Moonlit Sun are true hold-up horses pushed into a midfield representation, and of these, Rion Rubette's recent 7f Good-ground wins suggest she is most likely to secure a forward berth naturally, though all three face a harder task than their map position implies.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Hardy Warrior and Cristal Clere fight for the early lead and set a genuine but not suicidal gallop, allowing the prominent trackers to pounce.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners take the sting out of each other while Carolina Jetstream and Jagged Edge sit close enough to strike turning for home, with neither having burned energy in the lead battle. Good ground over a flat mile rewards exactly this profile — controlled speed, a strong sustained run from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Hardy Warrior breaks cleanly and asserts dominance early, forcing Cristal Clere to concede and settling into a controlled solo lead.
scenarios.body: DBM on Hardy Warrior has the class to establish a comfortable rhythm and find more in the straight if not pressed hard, using the flat track to his advantage at the top of the straight. The Joseph O'Brien yard is in strong form (7/57 over 14 days) and this scenario hands the race to the horse who controls their own destiny from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the front two run each other ragged and the pace genuinely burns up, creating an unusual late-race vacuum.
scenarios.body: Syzygy or Quebec, tracking from midfield to hold-up positions, could pick up the pieces if the leaders tie up, though Good ground at Killarney rarely collapses pace enough to gift true closers the race. This scenario is partially discounted because the redistributed hold-up horses (Subsonic, Rion Rubette, Moonlit Sun) are not truly racing from the deep position the map shows, reducing the volume of genuine late closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Produces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate enough that a midfield tracker who drops in quietly gets a perfect economical trip and produces a sustained run.
scenarios.body: Wearing Stars or Syzygy could benefit from a clean passage into the straight, with Wearing Stars showing strong course-and-distance form (2/8f/GOO, 4/8f/GOO) and catching the eye on a flat track if traffic is minimal. This scenario is the least likely because a contested early pace reduces the chance of a false-economy trip being available for stalkers at this distance.

watchPoints.text: Hardy Warrior and Cristal Clere — watch whether DBM pushes Hardy Warrior into an immediate, dominant lead at the first bend; if Cristal Clere concedes within the first furlong, the pace shape becomes a controlled solo lead rather than a contested burn, dramatically reducing the chance for prominent stalkers.

Rion Rubette — despite being mapped to midfield, Paddy Harnett may attempt to push her forward from stall six to reclaim her natural position near the pace; if she forces her way up, she adds a third genuine front-runner and could intensify the early pace sharply.

Quebec — the 89-day layoff is the longest in the field for a hold-up type that has never won beyond this distance; watch for her to be ridden quietly early and note whether she responds when asked, as a flat-track mile on Good ground in a run race is an examination she hasn't passed yet.

Subsonic — wearing a hood (tp) and dropping sharply in trip from 10f, watch whether Ben Coen positions her forward or settles mid-rear; if she gets agitated or fails to settle, the trip will expose her, but if she travels sweetly she could hit the board at a notable price.|

Wearing Stars (De Bromhead/Whelan) — the combination has fired four winners in 14 days; watch market moves close to post, as a supported Wearing Stars with a clean draw and a genuine pace to run at over her pet distance of 8f Good could make her the value play if the scenario unfolds cleanly.

races.name: T1 Healthcare Handicap

runners_data.name: Golddream
runners_data.note: The one genuine hold-up horse not redistributed on the map; David Marnane's 3yo wears a visor and has won at 8f on Good ground, and Luke McAteer will look to find cover before producing a late challenge — most viable closer in the field if any pace materialises.

runners_data.name: Saga Lucia
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner under Jamie Powell for an in-form O'Callaghan yard (2 wins last 14 days); limited recent form on turf Good (0W0P in 3 sim-going runs) is worth noting, but she owns the pace and that is a significant tactical advantage at this trip.

runners_data.name: Casamorati
runners_data.note: A Dylan Browne McMonagle booking lifts the eye but this JP O'Brien 3yo has faded in the finish repeatedly and has only two sim-going placed efforts from five attempts on similar ground, making it hard to be enthusiastic about her late prospects.

runners_data.name: Glitter And Glory
runners_data.note: Shane Foley's mount has the best sim-going strike rate in the field for a prominent runner (3 places from 8 similar-ground runs) and has been placed twice at 8f on Good at the highest end of her recent form — the natural second string to the leader and the most serious threat to Saga Lucia.

runners_data.name: Chapel Lane
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh takes over for McCreery and there is a 43-day absence to factor in; three places from six Good-ground runs suggest she stays competitive, but her tendency to race in mid-to-rear off slow fractions makes her dependent on others doing the donkey work up front.

runners_data.name: Sweet Baby Zou
runners_data.note: A 10f winner on Good for JP O'Brien last time, but her true inclination is to race from the rear and the map's placement of her in midfield reflects a crowded hold-up division rather than her natural role — her [STYLE_FIT] score of 0.91 signals the race shape is unlikely to suit, and the fade tendency compounds this.

runners_data.name: Only One Scobie
runners_data.note: Won at 8f on Heavy for Paul Flynn but her sim-going record on Good is poor (0W0P across 11 Good/similar-ground runs); in reality a hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield berth by the number of closers in this field, and Leigh Roche will struggle to find an angle unless the race falls apart in front.

runners_data.name: Chirac
runners_data.note: Paddy Harnett's 5lb claim is a solid booking for Feane's consistent 3yo, who has two top-four finishes at 8f on Good and a win at 7f on Soft last time; a genuine prominent racer whose price may be worth considering if he can sit handy and get a clear shot at the leaders in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Sancerre Rock
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery saddles his own horse after a 70-day break, and a 0/4 record on Good ground with a hood and tongue-tie combination rings no bells of confidence; naturally a hold-up racer placed in midfield on the map because of the overcrowded rear, making his task doubly difficult.

runners_data.name: John La Bear
runners_data.note: Ben Coen picks up this Ross O'Sullivan 3yo who won at 8f on Tapeta and has placed on Soft; a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield purely because of the glut of closers in this race, and the [STYLE_FIT] tag plus the fade flag mean the controlled pace set by Saga Lucia is the worst possible scenario for him.

races.paceDynamic: Saga Lucia is the one confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine pace rival likely to push from the outside, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the gates over Killarney's flat mile. The Good ground that has held all evening suits a race run at an honest but unspectacular tempo, meaning the lead is unlikely to be surrendered cheaply. Glitter And Glory and Chirac are the most natural prominent racers and will seek to sit just off Saga Lucia's shoulder, giving the pace a two-or-three horse front group with no chaos behind. This shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and produce a clean, progressive finish — those who must come from well off the pace face an uphill task in a race that will not fall apart in front. Several runners listed as midfield — Sweet Baby Zou, Only One Scobie, Sancerre Rock and John La Bear — are genuine hold-up types redistributed on the map because the field holds more back-of-the-field operators than the visual positions suggest; Saga Lucia, Glitter And Glory and Chirac are most likely to actually secure their natural front positions, and the race shape is firmly drawn in their favour.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Saga Lucia Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Saga Lucia establishes an uncontested lead and dictates a comfortable gallop that she never fully relinquishes.
scenarios.body: Saga Lucia bowls along in front on Good ground, rationing her effort through the middle part of the race and kicking again when challenged entering the final furlong; M D O'Callaghan has hit a purple patch (T14: 2/12) and Jamie Powell is booked to execute exactly this front-running plan.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Glitter And Glory or Chirac track Saga Lucia throughout and produce enough acceleration in the final two furlongs to collar her.
scenarios.body: Glitter And Glory's consistent Killarney-ground form (8/13 sim-going, three placed efforts) makes her the most dangerous prominent rival, and Shane Foley will sit just behind the pace before applying pressure at the two-furlong pole; if the tempo is even fractionally too slow, the prominent stalkers have the finishing kick to win a close finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fast enough to empty the leaders and a hold-up horse gets a clear run to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: Golddream is the most plausible beneficiary as the only hold-up horse not redistributed, carrying her own closing profile on Good ground (1W sim-going) and ridden by Luke McAteer who can switch her off early; however, given that most apparent closers in this field are not true hold-up types, the chance of a genuine late rush winning is constrained by the controlled pace Saga Lucia is expected to set.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Pace Plan
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners push forward aggressively at the start and force Saga Lucia into a faster-than-intended gallop that causes a messy, compressed finish.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace could see the field bunch leaving the back straight, giving midfield horses a slipstream and reducing the leader's advantage; even so, redistributed runners like Sweet Baby Zou and John La Bear face the compounded difficulty of racing genuinely out of position and against their natural instincts, limiting their upside even in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Glitter And Glory — Shane Foley is likely to position her right behind Saga Lucia from the off; if she tracks the leader without having to use extra petrol to do so, she becomes a serious danger in the final furlong on her consistent Good-ground form.

Saga Lucia's front-running record on turf Good is thin (0W0P from three sim-going runs) — watch for any signs of waywardness or sluggishness in the early stages that could allow Glitter And Glory or Chirac to move alongside before the straight.

Chirac and Glitter And Glory could jostle for the same prominent berth directly behind Saga Lucia, creating a minor traffic issue between the two prominent types and potentially gifting Golddream a gap on the outside in the final stages.

Sweet Baby Zou, Only One Scobie, Sancerre Rock and John La Bear are all genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield — if this group does not get an obvious split to aim for in the straight, their finishing efforts may neutralise each other rather than produce a clean run to the line.

The Good ground has been completely consistent across all seven races at Killarney this evening — no deterioration to factor in, and front-runners have been competitive throughout the card, reinforcing the pace-setting advantage Saga Lucia holds.

races.name: Kellihers Toyota Kingdom Gold Cup Handicap

runners_data.name: Taipan
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who sets the race up from the front with Shane Foley; his best form is over 14f-15f on Soft, making this Good ground over 1m6½f a slight concern, though he can control tempo; OR 96 is the highest in the field.

runners_data.name: Eagle Fang
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with an excellent recent Good-ground profile — four placings or wins from five on Good including a 1m4f victory — travels prominently and this trip and going look squarely in his wheelhouse; Chris Hayes is an astute judge of pace.

runners_data.name: Granite Bay
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for Jarlath Fahey ridden by apprentice Jack Cleary (5lb claim); has placed on Good ground at 1m6f+ and races prominently, and the claim helps offset the weight burden, though trainer's 14-day record is modest at 0/3.

runners_data.name: Royal Hollow
runners_data.note: Trainer-rider Andrew Slattery combination; a true hold-up horse who has finished second twice over similar distances on Good ground recently, and his 11-from-15 similar-going record shows he handles the conditions well, though he has yet to win from those placings.

runners_data.name: The Real Screamer
runners_data.note: Won twice at shorter (1m and 1m2f) on Good/Standard earlier in his campaign but was beaten into fourth on his only 1m6f start on Good; Ben Coen takes the ride and the step back up in trip is the key query.

runners_data.name: Factual Fact
runners_data.note: Useful Henry De Bromhead-trained seven-year-old who won over 1m5f on Good and placed over 1m4f; his natural game is to race prominently but the congested pace positions in this field make that difficult to secure — Ronan Whelan will need to adapt.

runners_data.name: Light Up The Dark
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's five-year-old with Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard; won over 1m4f on Soft and placed over 1m5f on Good, so the trip and going are broadly acceptable, though his Good-ground sample is limited at 5 from 10.

runners_data.name: War Rooms
runners_data.note: Won over 1m3f on Good last time out after a sequence of poor efforts at longer trips; a genuine hold-up type by nature with headgear worn previously, and Seamie Heffernan could produce him late, but his form at 1m6f+ is thin.

runners_data.name: Immutable
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll rides this Joseph Murphy-trained six-year-old who has twice finished second on Soft at 1m2f but has no wins on Good and his similar-going record is a stark 0 wins from 15 attempts — though his true running style is prominently inclined, he is pushed into midfield by the pace traffic ahead.

runners_data.name: Gaoth Chuil
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted at OR 77 with a 7lb claimer aboard; crucially, has won back-to-back over 1m5f and 1m7f on Good, making him one of the most proven horses in the race for today's conditions over this trip — a genuine hold-up type with live each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Luker's Tipple
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's five-year-old has won three times on Good ground at 1m6f-1m8f in recent starts, giving him arguably the strongest recent form profile for this precise race conditions; returned only 8 days ago, though, and his instinct is to race up with the pace — a position that will be hard to claim in this field.

runners_data.name: Sir Jeremy
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's four-year-old won over 1m2f on Good last time and goes with headgear; has won twice on Good overall but his best form is over shorter (1m-1m2f), making the 1m6½f trip a genuine stamina question at this stage of his career.

runners_data.name: Chutzpal
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's seven-year-old (second De Bromhead runner) wore headgear last time; has won at 1m4f-1m8f on Good ground, giving him solid course-type credentials, and his 14-from-15 similar-going record is standout — however, his age and OR of 74 reflect a horse who needs things to fall right.

races.paceDynamic: Taipan is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to press him hard from the outset, he should be able to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over this 1m6½f trip on Good ground at Killarney. Eagle Fang, Granite Bay, The Real Screamer and Light Up The Dark are all naturally prominent types who will look to race just off the pace, creating a compact, organised early order rather than a scramble. The field contains more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Factual Fact, Immutable, Luker's Tipple and Chutzpal are genuine prominent horses by inclination but are most likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield as Taipan, Eagle Fang, Granite Bay and The Real Screamer secure the natural positions closest to the pace. With one measured pace-setter and a steady Killarney gallop, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently without expending energy fighting for position, and who possess the stamina to sustain their effort through the final quarter-mile — prominent-to-midfield runners with proven Good-ground form at this sort of trip hold the clearest tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Taipan sets an unhurried, uncontested gallop and the prominent challengers track him into the straight with a controlled tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Taipan rolls along in front without ever being asked a serious question until the home turn, allowing the nearest pursuers to travel cheaply and produce sustained late efforts; horses who have tracked the pace without burning energy — particularly those with proven 1m6f+ Good-ground form — deliver their challenge with enough left in the tank to hold on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Exploit Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent bunch burn each other off chasing Taipan's steady splits and genuine hold-up horses find clear daylight in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Royal Hollow and Gaoth Chuil, genuine hold-up types who have each won at distances close to this on Good ground, are able to pick off the fading prominent runners with a sustained late run from the rear; War Rooms is another who could emerge late having settled well off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Taipan, untroubled throughout, produces a career-best in-front performance and the field fails to close the gap entering the straight.
scenarios.body: With Shane Foley able to control every aspect of the race from the front and a field that lacks a genuine pace-pusher, Taipan could simply extend clear when others begin their challenges; his Prominent tag and style-fit note temper the likelihood, but the lone-leader scenario on a flat, fair track cannot be ignored.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent glut causes early positional friction and an unexpected pace surge stretches the field, opening the door for a lower-rated runner at a big price.
scenarios.body: Luker's Tipple has won three of his last five on Good ground at today's sort of trip and, if he manages to secure a prominent berth despite his redistribution tag, possesses the form to trouble the favourites; Chutzpal has won at 1m6f+ on Good ground and cannot be entirely dismissed if he settles into a handy position against the odds.

watchPoints.text: Gaoth Chuil — back-to-back wins on Good over 1m5f-1m7f make him the most course-conditions-proven hold-up runner in the race; watch whether Reese Holohan (7) can slot him into a ground-saving position before launching his challenge.

Luker's Tipple — three recent Good-ground wins at 1m6f-1m8f give him outstanding form for this race, but he is only 8 days off his last run and will struggle to secure a prominent berth; if Gavin Cromwell has him fresh enough, he is a major player if he finds any position.

Eagle Fang — Chris Hayes has the experience to track Taipan closely and produce him at exactly the right moment; his nine-from-fifteen Good-ground record and four recent placings at this sort of trip make him the most consistent pace-shape beneficiary.

Taipan — watch the opening splits; if Shane Foley lets the race crawl from the front, the gallop will be too steady to shake off the closers, but if the early pace is genuinely unhurried it will suit the horse and compress the finish into a stamina test.

Factual Fact and Immutable — both are naturally prominent types who will be pushed wider or further back than ideal; if either manages to manoeuvre into a handy position early, their form entitles them to factor, but their redistribution into midfield is a significant tactical handicap.

races.name: Killarney Towers Hotel & Leisure Centre Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Lady Plimsoll
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form at distances up to 16f and ran well over this course trip last time; a hold-up operator in nature but shows enough tactical speed to sit closer if the pace is steady, and her recent good-ground form is solid.

runners_data.name: Trubshaw
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who can dictate terms without pressure; her one win came over 14f on good ground and the apprentice Gabriella Hill (7) claiming further relieves the burden — though she is technically racing at the top of her style-fit comfort zone, the absence of pace rivals makes that academic.

runners_data.name: Jurality
runners_data.note: Strong recent form including a win and multiple placings over 13-16f on good ground, and at 62 OR is well handicapped; a true hold-up horse whose best chance depends on the pace being strong enough to bring him late, though compression in the rear group may cost him a clear run.

runners_data.name: Numidia
runners_data.note: Two recent wins on good ground, most recently over 13f and 14f, and the tongue strap is retained; a genuine hold-up type whose chance improves sharply if the tempo is honest, and his course-going stats (2W2P from 5 sim-going runs) are notably positive.

runners_data.name: Charlie Brow'n
runners_data.note: Landed a win over 14f on soft ground but has been well beaten in his last two good-ground starts; a natural closer who has been bumped to a midfield position on the pace map because the field is congested with hold-up types, meaning he is unlikely to operate from his preferred deep position.

runners_data.name: Chicago Moon
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on good ground most recently and steps up sharply in trip here; a prominent-style horse whose fitness and yard form (De Bromhead T14: 4/38) are encouraging, and he is the most likely horse to press Trubshaw throughout.

runners_data.name: Espritroyale
runners_data.note: Back-to-back second-place finishes over 10f and 14f on soft and good ground respectively; a hold-up type with a rising profile and from the Gavin Cromwell yard (T14: 7/20), though he has yet to win and must prove he can sustain the effort over this longer 1m6½f trip.

runners_data.name: Desert Friend
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up specialist who has never won on good ground in his last five similar-going starts; bumped to a midfield position on the map because true closers are congested at the rear, and at OR=55 his chance looks limited without an extreme pace to exploit.

runners_data.name: Celestially
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 14f on good ground for Donnacha Aidan O'Brien and is bred to stay; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is further back than the map shows, having been shifted forward due to the volume of closers — the tongue strap is noted and she remains lightly campaigned.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Astolat
runners_data.note: Two placings at 12-14f on good ground suggest she stays and handles the surface; another true hold-up type displaced to midfield on the map by the congested field, and at OR=56 and with the 7lb claimer Kennedy, any improvement is needed to factor.

races.paceDynamic: Trubshaw is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m6½f handicap and, crucially, faces no serious pace pressure — with the rest of the field comprising genuine hold-up types or prominent racers who are unlikely to force the issue early over this stamina trip on good ground. Trubshaw can therefore dictate a controlled, honest gallop that plays entirely to her own strengths, setting a rhythm that will not be truly extreme in either direction but will be sustainable enough to expose those who need a strong pace to burn off. Chicago Moon holds a prominent style and is the most likely horse to accompany Trubshaw forward, while Lady Plimsoll shapes as the principal hold-up danger in behind. The field contains significantly more true hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Jurality, Celestially, Charlie Brow'n, Desert Friend and Queen Of Astolat are all genuine closers who will be bunched in midfield rather than in their natural rear positions, reducing their individual effectiveness and compressing the group that must find a way through. This race shape strongly favours the prominent and front-running profile: a controlled pace set by Trubshaw rewards those who can travel close to it and sustain the gallop, rather than those relying on a strong late injection.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trubshaw Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Trubshaw leads without meaningful pressure and Chicago Moon settles in second, the pace stays controlled and the leader conserves energy for a strong finish.
scenarios.body: Trubshaw dictates every yard, sets a measured gallop and simply refuses to be caught coming off the final bend with her stamina reserves intact; Chicago Moon, tracking in second throughout, is best placed to mount the only credible challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Sweeps Past
scenarios.trigger: If Trubshaw sets a pace that begins to empty in the final two furlongs, an attentive prominent or early-midfield mover picks her off.
scenarios.body: Lady Plimsoll, able to travel closer than her hold-up tag might suggest on this open galloping track, or Jurality if she secures a position better than her natural redistribution allows, produces a sustained run that swallows a fading Trubshaw late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Find Way Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely honest and the field strings out, one of the hold-up horses manages to thread a clear run and finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Numidia, with two recent wins on similar good going and a hold-up style that genuinely suits a strong pace, or Espritroyale, in excellent placing form at this trip on similar surfaces, gets the gaps to open and finishes best of all.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Produces Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls to the home turn and a sprint develops, hold-up horses are caught flat-footed and the race dissolves into a bunched finish.
scenarios.body: In a slow-run race any tactical advantage for Trubshaw evaporates; Charlie Brow'n or Celestially, if they manage to sit nearer the pace than their redistributed position suggests, could benefit from sheer positional luck in the rush.

watchPoints.text: Trubshaw — watch whether Chicago Moon attempts to race alongside her from the off; if De Bromhead's two runners split or if Chicago Moon goes with her, the front-running scenario weakens materially.

Jurality and Celestially — both genuine closers compressed into a midfield group; watch the draw and early positioning, as a bunched midfield will severely restrict their ability to produce a clean late run at Killarney's tight track.

Numidia — the visor is retained and his last two wins both came on good ground at this type of trip; if he gets a clear passage from the hold-up position, he is the most dangerous out-and-out closer in the field given his recent form.

Chicago Moon — stepping up significantly in trip (from 12f to 1m6½f) for the first time; watch how he travels into the home straight, as any sign of toiling will collapse Scenario B and leave Trubshaw with an uncontested lead.

races.name: HR Buddy (Q.R.) Race

runners_data.name: Murat
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner here and a two-time winner on Good ground; Mr H C Swan takes the ride for Peter Lawlor (winless last 14 days over four runs), but 43 days off and a good recent prep run puts him fresh enough to be dangerous if he dictates cleanly.

runners_data.name: Ragmans Corner
runners_data.note: Gerard Keane's seven-year-old won off this trip at Good going (17f, GOO) and the yard has had a runner place in the last 14 days; naturally a hold-up racer, he will likely find himself competing for cover further back than ideal, and his STYLE_FIT discount is real in a race where Murat controls from the front.

runners_data.name: Samui
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's lightly-raced seven-year-old (405 days off the track) returns wearing a tongue-tie and hood, and despite a strong record at Good going (three wins from 15 runners), the long layoff is a significant concern; prominent style suits this race shape if fitness holds.

runners_data.name: Can Happen
runners_data.note: The joint-top-rated runner (OR 120) has won on Good ground at 16f and is equipped with a tongue-tie, but Miss Georgie Benson (7lb claim) has just one run to draw on in this form string; a genuine hold-up racer who needs the pace to collapse late, which is a low-probability outcome when Murat leads alone.

runners_data.name: Glowing Account
runners_data.note: Mullins sends this OR 120 nine-year-old out 23 days after a flat-track return (finished 15th, 12f, Good), and the step back up to 2m1f suits a horse that won over 16f on Good ground; prominent style is well-placed in this race shape, but the poor recent run needs explaining.

runners_data.name: Silas Marner
runners_data.note: Sabrina Harty's nine-year-old ran just eight days ago and carries the lowest competitive OR (48) in the field; a true hold-up type shuffled into the midfield grouping on the map, his recent form figures of 9-18-16 at Good going make him very hard to support at this level even if he gets a clear run.

runners_data.name: Simpletwistoffaith
runners_data.note: John O'Neill's nine-year-old returns after 294 days off (last run August 2024) having failed to win from 15 outings on Good ground; a hold-up racer by nature, the extended absence and poor form figures (9-6-11-8-13) over staying trips make him extremely difficult to recommend in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Supreme Law
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner (OR 40) in the race, tagged as one who fades in the finish and flagged as racing out of natural role even when mapped to midfield; Harty's stable has had no winners from two runs in the last 14 days, and a finishing pattern of fade-late means this race shape actively works against him.

races.paceDynamic: Murat is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no other natural pace-setter to challenge him, he is virtually certain to dictate terms at whatever tempo suits him over the 2m1f trip on Good ground at Killarney. With freedom to control, Murat can set a measured, sustainable gallop that keeps the race honest but avoids the kind of suicidal fractions that would cut his own throat, giving him every chance to steal an unassailable lead turning for home. The hold-up contingent — Can Happen, Simpletwistoffaith, Ragmans Corner, Silas Marner, and Supreme Law — will be chasing from off the pace, and Glowing Account and Samui will look to slot in behind Murat from prominent positions. This race shape strongly favours front-running and prominent racers: a lone pace-setter on Good ground over a strongly-run staying trip in a field that lacks a genuine pace antagonist is the textbook scenario for a horse to lead and outstay the field. Note that the field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear; Ragmans Corner, Silas Marner, and Supreme Law are redistributed into midfield on the map, but their true preference is for a late challenge — in a race Murat controls from the front, those horses will need things to go wrong for the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Murat Leads, Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Murat breaks cleanly and immediately establishes an uncontested lead, setting a comfortable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Murat controls fractions entirely, denying his rivals a target until late, and his good-ground form (two wins at this going code) makes him dangerous over this C&D trip; a well-judged, front-running ride for Mr H C Swan could see him simply outstay a field that cannot close quickly enough.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If Murat sets a pace just fractionally too generous and Samui or Glowing Account press him relentlessly from the turn.
scenarios.body: Samui (OR 104, three wins in good-ground conditions) or Glowing Account (Mullins-trained, OR 120, recent win on Good) have the class to pick Murat off if he has given too much early; the prominent runners stay close enough throughout to produce a sustained finish that rewards class over pure speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Murat sets an unexpectedly strong pace that strings the field out and opens the race up for a well-timed late run.
scenarios.body: Can Happen (OR 120, proven on Good, ridden by amateur Miss Georgie Benson) is the highest-rated hold-up runner and has tactical scope, while Ragmans Corner has shown a winning run from off the pace; both need the tempo to be genuinely testing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Late
scenarios.trigger: If Murat sets a very slow pace that produces a bunched, sprint-like finish over the final two fences.
scenarios.body: In a slowly-run affair the field closes in a heap and the race becomes a matter of who jumps best in the home straight; Glowing Account and Can Happen carry the highest ratings (both OR 120) and would have the class edge in a tactical lottery, but amateur jockeys and fitness queries add uncertainty throughout.

watchPoints.text: Murat's jumping must be monitored from the first fence — if he makes an early error and loses his uncontested lead, the entire race shape collapses and the prominent pair Samui and Glowing Account become the primary threats.

Samui's 405-day absence is a serious fitness flag; if Gordon Elliott has this horse ready first time back, Ms Hannah Smullen's claim could prove significant, but any sign of greenness or weakness in the home straight should be noted early.

Glowing Account's latest run (15th, 12f, Flat, Good) is strikingly poor for a Mullins-trained OR 120 horse — watch for whether this was a schooling spin or a genuine form concern, as the step up in trip may be the explanation.

Can Happen is the highest-rated hold-up horse and shapes as the most dangerous closer if anything goes wrong up front, but Miss Georgie Benson's limited experience over these fences means positional errors in the closing stages are a real possibility.

Silas Marner and Supreme Law are both trained by Sabrina Harty and run just 8 and 15 days apart respectively — watch for any stable-team riding instructions that might affect how the race unfolds positionally, even if neither is a realistic winning chance.
